Technical / Mathematical Description: Resistor: v = i*R (Ohm's law), power p = i^2*R. Inductor: v = L*di/dt, stored energy = (1/2)*L*i^2. Capacitor: i = C*dv/dt, stored energy = (1/2)*C*v^2.

Sub-Topic / Heading: Voltage and Current Sources; Source Transformation
Technical / Mathematical Description: An ideal voltage source keeps terminal voltage fixed irrespective of current; an ideal current source keeps current fixed. A practical voltage source Vs in series with Rs is equivalent to a current source Is = Vs/Rs in parallel with the same Rs (and vice versa).
Series: R_eq = R1 + R2 + ... + Rn (same current). Parallel: 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... + 1/Rn (same voltage); for two resistors R_eq = R1*R2/(R1 + R2).

Sub-Topic / Heading: Voltage Divider and Current Divider Rules
Technical / Mathematical Description: Voltage divider: V_k = Vs * R_k/(R1 + R2 + ... + Rn) across resistor R_k in series. Current divider (two parallel branches): I1 = I_total * R2/(R1 + R2), I2 = I_total * R1/(R1 + R2).
KCL: algebraic sum of currents at a node = 0 (current in = current out). KVL: algebraic sum of voltage rises and drops around any closed loop = 0.

Assign a loop current to each mesh, apply KVL around each mesh and solve the simultaneous equations, written in matrix form as [R][I] = [V], where diagonal terms are the total resistance of the mesh and off-diagonal terms are minus the shared resistance.
Choose a reference (ground) node, apply KCL at each remaining node with branch current = (V_node - V_adjacent)/R, and solve [G][V] = [I], where G is the conductance matrix (G = 1/R).

In a linear bilateral network with several independent sources, the response (current or voltage) equals the algebraic sum of responses due to each source acting alone, with other voltage sources short-circuited and other current sources open-circuited.

Any linear two-terminal network can be replaced by a voltage source V_th in series with R_th, where V_th = open-circuit voltage across the terminals and R_th = resistance seen from the terminals with independent sources deactivated. Load current I_L = V_th/(R_th + R_L).

Any linear two-terminal network can be replaced by a current source I_N in parallel with R_N, where I_N = short-circuit current across the terminals and R_N = R_th. Load current I_L = I_N*R_N/(R_N + R_L); conversion: V_th = I_N*R_N.

Sub-Topic / Heading: Time-Domain Analysis of First-Order RL Circuit
Technical / Mathematical Description: Time constant tau = L/R. Growth of current (switch closed): i(t) = (V/R)*(1 - e^(-t/tau)); reaches about 63.2% of final value at t = tau. Decay of current: i(t) = I0*e^(-t/tau); falls to about 36.8% of I0 at t = tau.
A coil of N turns, area A, rotating at angular speed omega in a uniform field B generates e = N*B*A*omega*sin(omega*t) = Em*sin(omega*t), with omega = 2*pi*f.
Waveform, cycle, time period T and frequency f = 1/T; instantaneous value v = Vm*sin(omega*t +/- phi); phase and phase difference phi between two sinusoids (leading/lagging).

Sub-Topic / Heading: RMS and Average Value of a Sine Wave
Technical / Mathematical Description: V_rms = Vm/sqrt(2) = 0.707*Vm; V_avg (half cycle) = 2*Vm/pi = 0.637*Vm; form factor = V_rms/V_avg = 1.11; peak factor = Vm/V_rms = 1.414.
Rectangular: V = a + jb. Polar: V = |V| angle(theta), where |V| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) and theta = tan^-1(b/a); conversion a = |V|*cos(theta), b = |V|*sin(theta).

Sub-Topic / Heading: AC Circuits with Pure R, Pure L and Pure C
Technical / Mathematical Description: R: v and i in phase, P = V*I. L: X_L = omega*L = 2*pi*f*L, current lags voltage by 90 deg, average power = 0. C: X_C = 1/(omega*C), current leads voltage by 90 deg, average power = 0. Power factor = 1, 0 lag, 0 lead respectively.
Z = R + jX_L, |Z| = sqrt(R^2 + X_L^2), phase angle phi = tan^-1(X_L/R) (current lags), I = V/|Z|, P = V*I*cos(phi), power factor = R/|Z| lagging.
Z = R - jX_C, |Z| = sqrt(R^2 + X_C^2), phi = tan^-1(X_C/R) (current leads), I = V/|Z|, P = V*I*cos(phi), power factor = R/|Z| leading.
Z = R + j(X_L - X_C), |Z| = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2). X_L > X_C: inductive, current lags. X_L < X_C: capacitive, current leads. X_L = X_C: resonance, Z = R, pf = 1.
Resonant frequency f0 = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C)); at resonance Z = R (minimum), I = V/R (maximum), pf = 1. Quality factor Q = omega0*L/R = (1/R)*sqrt(L/C); bandwidth BW = f2 - f1 = f0/Q.

For an ideal parallel L-C circuit, f0 = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C)); at resonance impedance is maximum and line current is minimum. For a practical coil of resistance R, f0 = (1/(2*pi))*sqrt(1/(L*C) - R^2/L^2).

Sub-Topic / Heading: Polyphase System and Advantages of Three-Phase
Technical / Mathematical Description: Three voltages of equal magnitude displaced by 120 deg: e_R = Em*sin(wt), e_Y = Em*sin(wt - 120 deg), e_B = Em*sin(wt + 120 deg). Advantages: constant instantaneous power, smaller conductor size for the same power, self-starting motors, higher efficiency.
V_L = sqrt(3)*V_ph (line voltage leads phase voltage by 30 deg), I_L = I_ph. Total power P = 3*V_ph*I_ph*cos(phi) = sqrt(3)*V_L*I_L*cos(phi).
V_L = V_ph, I_L = sqrt(3)*I_ph. Total power P = 3*V_ph*I_ph*cos(phi) = sqrt(3)*V_L*I_L*cos(phi).

A static device transferring power between two windings on a common laminated core by mutual induction (Faraday's law) at the same frequency. An alternating flux set up by the primary induces an EMF in the secondary.
E1 = 4.44*f*N1*phi_m and E2 = 4.44*f*N2*phi_m, where phi_m = B_m*A_core is the peak core flux (derived from E_rms = 4*f*N*phi_m*form factor, form factor = 1.11).
K = N2/N1 = E2/E1 = V2/V1 = I1/I2. Rated VA = V1*I1 = V2*I2, so full-load current I = (kVA rating * 1000)/V for the respective winding.

Voltage regulation (%) = (V_no-load - V_full-load)/V_no-load * 100. Efficiency eta = output power/(output power + P_iron + P_cu). Maximum efficiency occurs when variable (copper) loss = constant (iron) loss, i.e. x^2*P_cu,fl = P_i.

Sub-Topic / Heading: Ideal vs Practical Transformer, Losses and Equivalent Circuit
Technical / Mathematical Description: Ideal: no losses, no leakage flux, infinite core permeability. Practical losses: iron loss (hysteresis, proportional to f*B_m^1.6, and eddy current, proportional to f^2*B_m^2*t^2) and copper loss (I^2*R). Equivalent circuit uses R1, X1, R2, X2 and the no-load branch R0 || X0.

Sub-Topic / Heading: DC Motor: Construction, Working, Types and Applications
Technical / Mathematical Description: Parts: field poles, armature, commutator, brushes. A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences force F = B*I*l (Fleming's left-hand rule). Back EMF E_b = V - I_a*R_a; torque T is proportional to phi*I_a. Shunt motor: field in parallel with armature (nearly constant speed). Series motor: field in series (high starting torque).

A balanced 3-phase stator winding produces a rotating magnetic field at synchronous speed N_s = 120*f/P rpm. Rotor speed N_r = N_s*(1 - s), where slip s = (N_s - N_r)/N_s. Rotor is squirrel-cage or wound type; applications include pumps, fans, conveyors.

A single-phase winding produces a pulsating (not rotating) field, so the motor is not self-starting; split-phase or capacitor-start auxiliary winding creates the starting torque. Synchronous speed N_s = 120*f/P; applications include fans, washing machines, small pumps.
Diode current I = I0*(e^(V/(n*V_T)) - 1), with thermal voltage V_T = kT/q (about 26 mV at 300 K). Cut-in voltage is about 0.7 V (Si) and 0.3 V (Ge); conducts in forward bias, blocks in reverse bias.
For input v = Vm*sin(wt): V_dc = Vm/pi, V_rms = Vm/2, ripple factor = 1.21, maximum efficiency = 40.6%, PIV = Vm, ripple frequency = f.
V_dc = 2*Vm/pi, V_rms = Vm/sqrt(2), ripple factor = 0.482, maximum efficiency = 81.2%, ripple frequency = 2f; PIV = Vm (bridge) or 2*Vm (centre-tap).
Zener operates in reverse breakdown with nearly constant voltage V_Z. As a shunt regulator: I_total = (V_in - V_Z)/R_s = I_Z + I_L, so R_s = (V_in - V_Z)/(I_Z + I_L).

I_E = I_B + I_C and I_C = beta*I_B in the active region. As a switch: cut-off gives output about V_CC (OFF), saturation gives output about V_CE(sat) = 0.2 V (ON), so the output is the inverse of the input.

LED emits photons on recombination (E = h*f); photodiode (reverse biased) gives photocurrent proportional to light intensity; solar cell converts light directly into electrical power; opto-coupler = LED + photodetector providing electrical isolation.
A device converting one form of energy into another (usually a physical quantity to an electrical signal). Block diagram: measurand -> sensing element -> transduction element -> electrical output.

Sub-Topic / Heading: Operational Amplifier: Inverting and Non-Inverting Amplifier
Technical / Mathematical Description: Ideal op-amp: A = infinity, R_in = infinity, R_out = 0, V+ = V-. Inverting: V_out = -(R_f/R_1)*V_in. Non-inverting: V_out = (1 + R_f/R_1)*V_in.

Sub-Topic / Heading: Op-Amp as Comparator and RC Phase-Shift Oscillator
Technical / Mathematical Description: Comparator: V_out = +V_sat if V+ > V-, else -V_sat. RC phase-shift oscillator: three RC sections give 180 deg phase shift with inverting amplifier giving 180 deg; f = 1/(2*pi*R*C*sqrt(6)) and gain must be at least 29.
8-pin IC: 1 GND, 2 Trigger, 3 Output, 4 Reset, 5 Control, 6 Threshold, 7 Discharge, 8 V_CC. In monostable mode a trigger below V_CC/3 produces one output pulse of width T = 1.1*R*C.
AND: Y = A.B (1 only if all inputs are 1). OR: Y = A + B (1 if any input is 1). NOT: Y = A' (inverts the input). Each described by a truth table and gate symbol.
(A.B)' = A' + B' and (A + B)' = A'.B'; the complement of an AND equals the OR of complements, and vice versa.
NAND: Y = (A.B)'. NOR: Y = (A + B)'. Any Boolean function can be realised using only NAND gates or only NOR gates.
XOR: Y = A xor B = A'.B + A.B' (1 when inputs differ). XNOR: Y = (A xor B)' = A.B + A'.B' (1 when inputs are equal).

Identity: A + 0 = A, A.1 = A. Null: A + 1 = 1, A.0 = 0. Idempotent: A + A = A. Complement: A + A' = 1, A.A' = 0. Involution: (A')' = A. Commutative, associative, distributive, and absorption: A + A.B = A.
SOP: OR of AND terms (e.g. Y = A.B + A'.C). POS: AND of OR terms (e.g. Y = (A + B).(A' + C)). Expressions are simplified using Boolean laws and implemented with basic gates.
Adds two 1-bit numbers: Sum = A xor B, Carry = A.B.
Adds two bits plus carry-in: Sum = A xor B xor Cin, Cout = A.B + Cin.(A xor B) = A.B + B.Cin + A.Cin.
Many-to-one data selector: 2^n data inputs, n select lines, one output. 2:1: Y = S'.D0 + S.D1. 4:1 uses 2 select lines, 8:1 uses 3.
One-to-many distributor: one data input routed to one of 2^n outputs by n select lines. 1:2: Y0 = D.S', Y1 = D.S.
n-bit converter step size (resolution) = V_FS/2^n. ADC maps an analog voltage to a digital code (D = V_in/step); DAC produces V_out = D * step from digital code D.
